nota: Real lunar missions (EXTERNAL data: not on the challenge's official list; simplified summaries — check the agencies' sites for details). Entries unlock as the story advances.

misiones.resumen: First human-made object to reach the Moon, by impacting its surface.
misiones.leccion: Every lunar program started by simply reaching the Moon.

misiones.resumen: First soft landing on the Moon and first photos from its surface.
misiones.leccion: It proved the ground could hold a lander: your base stands on that idea.

misiones.tripulacion: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins
misiones.resumen: First crewed landing, at Tranquility Base. Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the surface while Collins orbited.
misiones.leccion: A crew of three, each with a role — like the four mission segments in this game.

misiones.tripulacion: Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, Fred Haise
misiones.resumen: An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon. The landing was cancelled and the crew came home safely using the lunar module as a lifeboat.
misiones.leccion: Called a 'successful failure': improvising with what you have, like sealing leaks with scrap.

misiones.resumen: Detected hydrogen signals at the lunar poles, a hint of water ice hiding in cold craters.
misiones.leccion: Why you look for ice in the shadowed crater.

misiones.resumen: Crashed a rocket stage into Cabeus crater near the south pole and found water in the debris plume.
misiones.leccion: Real evidence of water ice near the south pole — your fuel source.

misiones.tripulacion: Gus Grissom, Ed White, Roger Chaffee
misiones.resumen: A cabin fire during a ground test killed the crew. NASA redesigned the spacecraft and its safety procedures.
misiones.leccion: Heat and fire are deadly in a spacecraft: respect the Scorch Fields and your suit's limits.

misiones.resumen: First US soft landing. It tested the landing techniques Apollo would later use.
misiones.leccion: Testing systems before trusting them — like checking every rocket subsystem.

misiones.resumen: First privately funded lunar lander attempt. A problem during descent shut down the main engine and it crashed.
misiones.leccion: One failing subsystem can end a mission: repair them all before you launch.

misiones.resumen: The Vikram lander crashed during its final descent, but the orbiter kept working and returning science.
misiones.leccion: A mission can partly fail and still succeed in other ways.

misiones.resumen: First soft landing on the far side of the Moon. It talked to Earth through the Queqiao relay satellite.
misiones.leccion: Exactly what your CubeSat relay does when there's no direct line to Earth.

misiones.resumen: First landing in the lunar south polar region, where you are stranded.
misiones.leccion: The south pole is the new frontier because of its ice.

misiones.resumen: Crashed into the Moon after a problem during an orbital maneuver, days before it was meant to land.
misiones.leccion: Burns and trajectories must be right: that's why return windows matter.

misiones.resumen: Landed with pinpoint precision but tipped over; it still worked when sunlight reached its solar panels.
misiones.leccion: Solar power can bring a mission back to life — keep your panels working.

misiones.tripulacion: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, Bill Anders
misiones.resumen: First crew to orbit the Moon. Anders took the famous 'Earthrise' photo.
misiones.leccion: Seeing Earth from the Moon changed how people saw their planet.

misiones.tripulacion: Eugene Cernan, Harrison Schmitt, Ronald Evans
misiones.resumen: The last crewed landing of the Apollo era. Schmitt was the first scientist (a geologist) to walk on the Moon.
misiones.leccion: Scientists in the field: the 'user segment' of a mission.

misiones.resumen: The Orion spacecraft flew around the Moon on the SLS rocket and returned to Earth.
misiones.leccion: SLS burns liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen — the same propellants you make from ice.

misiones.tripulacion: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen
misiones.resumen: First crewed flight of Orion, around the Moon and back. Check NASA for the latest status.
misiones.leccion: The next generation of lunar explorers — maybe you.
